carriedFindings.XV5-1: carried (NOTE, round 5) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: Invariant (c) ('never an entrypoint, for any domain') now rests on the type's `category` field. Reclassify the interpreter as ENTRYPOINT, grant it to an unclosed domain, and nothing catches it. So the dropped A77.planeon_interpreter_exec_t was not unable to fail.
carriedFindings.XV6-3: carried (NOTE, round 6) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: _cleanup_grant maps each socket-file type to one listener through a dict built over `sockets`. If two socket rows name the same file type, only the last row's listener counts, and check_matrix does not require one socket row per socket-file type.
carriedFindings.XV6-6: carried (NOTE, round 6) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: The removal works under the pinned matrix, and the matrix closes no permission it needs. Two premises are worth stating. (a) Q106-Q109 pin only dir search, write, remove_name and rmdir. The cleanup also opens, lists and stats the directory (dir open, read, getattr); init_t's unconditional v5 READ on planeon_run_t grants these, but no check pins them. (b) The directory type. systemd creates RuntimeDirectory= paths with its label-aware mkdir, which sets an fscreate context from the loaded file contexts, and selinux_determine_inode_label prefers that fscreate SID over a named type transition or inheritance. So /run/planeon, live-proxy and maintenance carry planeon_run_t only if W03's file contexts say so, while README:661-668 names only the named type transition for systemd's /run/planeon. By my reading, a base-policy /run/.* entry would otherwise give var_run_t, and host policy would then decide the cleanup.
carriedFindings.XV7-1: carried (NOTE, round 7) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: A79.<type> now covers EXECUTE and EXECMOD, as Q-MX6-R6 (b) decided. It still leaves out execute_no_trans. Its statement ('systemd may only stat and unlink ...', matrix.json:7102, 7174, 7246, 7318) and the README Assertions row ('may do nothing else to it', README:762) therefore claim one permission more than the assertion pins.
carriedFindings.XV7-2: carried (NOTE, round 7) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: The XV6-2 fix is correct: a narrowed grant no longer counts as WRITE, M116 is refused, and candidate 5's behaviour is restored. The rule asks whether a WRITE entry reaches 'dir add_name'. It does not ask whether the parent type labels directories, as allowed() does (line 158: cls in entry['classes']). README:89-90 ('needs dir add_name on the parent') is therefore slightly stronger than the code.
carriedFindings.XV7-3: carried (NOTE, round 7) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: Two docstrings did not follow the XV6-2 change. The module docstring's list of extensions to v5 (lines 8-25) does not mention that v5's named-type-transition rule now uses _granted_file. REVIEW_BRIEF.md:125-127 question 1 uses that list as the yardstick. _granted_file's docstring still describes only 'a narrowed READ entry ... (v5)', but the function now also serves this WRITE check and the candidate-6 narrowed WRITE shape.
carriedFindings.XV7-4: carried (NOTE, round 7) to the matrix v6 packet review or a later matrix revision: The round-6 disposition rows for XV6-3 and XV6-6 (README:417, 420) point to records outside the subject. 'Carried (status)' points to a status.json that architecture/selinux-matrix-v4 does not yet have at d45a0d8b.
